Shared laws, commands and teaching applying to all within the stated audience or conditions. General does not remove covenant, historical, priestly or household limits. Read the existing Transformed, Fulfilled, Unchanged, Everlasting and other classifications alongside each entry.

Some source records still need their audience resolved. These are explicitly marked audience review pending; their provisional filing here is not a claim that they apply universally. Passage groups may contain both shared teaching and personal directions.

General · Personal · Instructions overview

3,869 study records in this view. Entries can overlap; this is not a count of distinct biblical commands. Ordered by the first source book, chapter and verse.

The source wording follows the Saints Greek-English text: the Septuagint for the Old Testament and the Greek New Testament. Headings and application notes are study summaries. Preserve the passage’s speaker, audience, conditions and grammatical form. Source alignment checked 6 November 2026; independent critical-Greek review remains in progress.

S156 · Levirate marriage in an Israelite household

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

25:5 And if brethren dwell together, and one of them dies, and has no seed, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside unto a man who is not near of kin. Her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her unto himself for a wife, and dwell with her as husband.

25:6 And it shall be, that the child whom she bears shall be established in the name of the dead, and his name shall not be blotted out of Israel.

25:7 And if the man will not take his brother’s wife, the woman shall go up unto the gate, unto the elders, and say: My husband’s brother will not raise up his brother’s name in Israel; my husband’s brother has refused.

25:8 And the elders of his city shall call him, and speak unto him; and if he stands and says: I will not take her,

25:9 then his brother’s wife shall draw near before the elders, and loose one sandal from his foot, and spit in his face, and answer and say: Thus shall they do unto the man who will not build up his brother’s house.

25:10 And his name shall be called in Israel: The House of Him Whose Sandal Was Loosed.

Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.

Classification: Study context · Topical study

Topic: Marriage, family and care for parents

Original scope: Text and setting: Family and inheritance law

Connection to Christ: Jesus discusses levirate marriage in a resurrection dispute, while Paul speaks of a widow’s freedom to marry in the Lord. Christian response today: Respect widows and do not impose this ancient household arrangement as a universal marriage obligation.
